card.name: Ojapali
card.tagline: Assamese narrative song-and-dance led by an oja and chorus
card.profile: Ojapali is an Assamese narrative song-dance tradition performed by an ensemble led by an 'oja' (lead) supported by 'pali' (chorus), blending sung narration, dialogue, gesture and semi-improvised dramatisation, accompanied mainly by small cymbals (khutitaal) (Wikipedia). Scholars trace its roots to the pan-Indian kathakata (epic storytelling) tradition, dating its development well before Assam's neo-Vaishnavite movement; Darrang district (Mangaldai, Sipajhar) is considered a historical hub, patronised under King Dharmanarayana (1615-1637) (Wikipedia). Its strands include epic-based forms (Assamese Ramayana and Mahabharata) and Sukananni/Maroi Goa Ojapali rooted in Shakta (Shakti) worship, with Vyah Goa Ojapali belonging to the Vaishnava cult (Wikipedia; Gkseries).
card.insight: Ojapali is widely regarded as a precursor that influenced Srimanta Sankaradeva's theatrical idiom (Ankiya Naat/Bhaona) and Sattriya dance; the Sangeet Natak Akademi has recognised exponents such as Lalit Chandra Nath (Award 1983) and Kinaram Nath Oja (Award 2012, Suknani Ojapali) (Wikipedia; Sangeet Natak Akademi).
card.image_significance: Assam's oldest narrative song-dance. A representative image shows ornate costume and expressive hand-gesture (mudra) detail — Assam (Darrang), India.
